The meeting focused on the GraphQL Federation specification, particularly the naming and technical details around interface objects and overrides. Michael, David, and Pascal discussed renaming the specification to "GraphQL Federation Specification," with the group generally in favor but raising potential confusion with Apollo Federation. They delved into the technicalities of interface objects, questioning certain restrictions in Apollo Federation, such as not allowing implementations in the same subgraph as the interface object. ## Summary

### GraphQL Federation Specification Discussion

Michael discussed work on interface object comments and encouraged community input through pull requests for the specification text. The team discussed a potential new GraphQL primitive for handling interface objects, with Pascal noting that introducing new type system members is challenging due to their widespread impact. Michael announced that the final specification name will be "GraphQL Federation Specification" and that the working title "Composite Schema specification" would be completed that evening.

### GraphQL Federation Industry Standard Adoption

The group discussed adopting the term "GraphQL Federation" as an industry standard to complement Apollo Federation. David expressed concern about potential confusion between different federation specifications, but agreed with the proposal after Michael clarified that the new specification would extend Apollo Federation rather than replace it. Michael explained that while Apollo would continue developing their version, the GraphQL community would take over leadership of the federation specification going forward, with the goal of completing the standard this year and updating the foundation's federation pages to reflect all implementing vendors.

### GraphQL Federation Implementation Discussion

Michael led a discussion about GraphQL Federation specifications, focusing on interface objects and implementation directives. The team debated the naming and functionality of the implements directive, with David advocating for "override" based on its inheritance-like behavior, while Michael preferred "implements" due to naming conflicts with existing "override" functionality. They also discussed concerns about the Apollo Federation approach to progressive overrides through labels, with David and Pascal arguing that traffic routing policies should be handled at the gateway level rather than in the schema itself, as it creates unnecessary deployment complexity. The group agreed to further consider the implementation approach and potentially involve Sachin from Apollo in future discussions to better understand their reasoning behind the current implementation.
